label: Global-South Consumer Financial Protection
description: Assess consumer financial protection issues in Global-South markets — digital-lending abuse, mobile-money redress, pricing transparency, over-indebtedness, and data privacy — against representative national regimes (Kenya, Nigeria, Bangladesh, India) and the realities of thin-regulation, ADR, and informal-justice settings.

claudeKnowledge.description: Kenya Consumer Protection Act 2012 + CBK consumer-protection guidelines & Digital Credit Providers Regulations 2022; Nigeria FCCPA 2018 + CBN Consumer Protection Framework 2016 / Consumer Protection Regulations 2019 + FCCPC Limited Interim Framework for Digital Lending 2022; Bangladesh Consumer Rights Protection Act 2009 + Bangladesh Bank guidelines; India Consumer Protection Act 2019 + RBI Digital Lending Guidelines 2022 + RBI Fair Practices Code; mobile-money / EMI consumer-redress rules; data-protection statutes (Kenya DPA 2019, Nigeria NDPA 2023, India DPDP Act 2023 + DPDP Rules 2025, Bangladesh PDPO 2025 — enforcement deferred to ~mid-2027); GSMA / CGAP / SMART Campaign / FATF financial-inclusion guidance.

guidedInputs.label: Market / Jurisdiction
guidedInputs.description: Which national consumer-finance regime(s) apply? Each anchors a different statutory and supervisory baseline.

guidedInputs.label: Provider / Product Type
guidedInputs.description: What kind of financial provider or product is the consumer dealing with? Drives which conduct rules and redress channels apply.

guidedInputs.label: Consumer-Harm Areas
guidedInputs.description: Which harms or protection themes should the assessment prioritise?

guidedInputs.label: Your Role
guidedInputs.description: Who is this assessment for? Shapes whether the output is advocacy-facing or provider-remediation-facing.

guidedInputs.label: Known Issues or Concerns
guidedInputs.description: Describe the specific situation, complaint, product terms, or conduct pattern — and any documents available (loan agreement, SMS/screenshots, statements, prior complaint correspondence).
guidedInputs.placeholder: e.g. App-based lender charged a 'service fee' that doubled the headline interest; on a 3-day default they messaged my phone contacts. Loan agreement (screenshot) and call-log available. I want to know what rules were broken and where to complain.

exampleInput: I run a consumer-advocacy clinic in Nairobi and we're seeing a wave of complaints against a Kenyan app-based digital lender. Typical fact pattern: a borrower takes a KES 5,000 loan advertised as '7-day, low cost'; the headline interest is quoted as a flat fee, but a 'processing fee' and 'rollover fee' push the effective cost well above 100% APR with nothing disclosed as an annualised rate. On a 2-day default the app sends SMS to the borrower's phone contacts ('debt-shaming') and threatens to report them to the CRBs. The app pulled the full contact list and SMS inbox at install. The lender is a registered Digital Credit Provider. Assess this against Kenyan law and CBK rules — Consumer Protection Act 2012, the CBK Digital Credit Providers Regulations 2022, and the Data Protection Act 2019 — tell me which conduct is a statutory breach versus a guideline breach, and map the redress routes (CBK, ODPC, Competition Authority, small claims, ADR). Known weak spots in our case file: we have screenshots and the loan agreement, but no signed proof the borrower consented to contact-list access.

exampleValues.known_concerns: Effective cost >100% with no APR disclosed; debt-shaming SMS to the borrower's contacts on a 2-day default; full contact-list + SMS-inbox harvesting at install. Lender is a registered DCP. We hold screenshots and the loan agreement but no signed consent for contact-list access.
